questions.concept: Standalone Agent helpers append durable messages without generation
questions.context:
Convex 1.41.0, Agent 0.6.4, ai 6.0.229, provider-utils 4.0.39, convex-helpers 0.1.120. The app schema is empty and the Agent component is mounted. Source-provided helper signatures: `createThread(ctx, components.agent, { userId, title })` returns a thread ID; `saveMessage(ctx, components.agent, { threadId, message: { role, content } })` saves a message; `listMessages(ctx, components.agent, { threadId, paginationOpts })` returns `{ page, isDone, continueCursor }`. These standalone helpers need no Agent instance or model provider.

A mutation creates one thread. Two subsequent mutations call saveMessage for that same thread ID: first `{ role: "user", content: "m1" }`, then `{ role: "assistant", content: "m2" }`. No generation method is called.
questions.question: What is stored in that thread after both mutations commit?

options.text: Only m2; saving with the same threadId replaces the earlier message.
options.rationale: threadId identifies the conversation, not a message upsert key. Both saves append.

options.text: Only m1; an assistant message is persisted only after model generation.
options.rationale: The standalone helper directly accepts an assistant message; generation is unnecessary.

options.text: Both m1 and m2, with their supplied roles.
options.rationale: Both standalone saves append durable component messages, independent of any model.

options.text: Nothing; the helpers buffer messages until an Agent generates a reply.
options.rationale: The standalone helper performs durable component mutations immediately within the transaction.

questions.concept: Agent pagination continues with its opaque component cursor
questions.context:
Convex 1.41.0, Agent 0.6.4, ai 6.0.229, provider-utils 4.0.39, convex-helpers 0.1.120. Source-provided helper signatures: `createThread(ctx, components.agent, { userId, title })` returns a thread ID; `saveMessage(ctx, components.agent, { threadId, message: { role, content } })` saves a message; `listMessages(ctx, components.agent, { threadId, paginationOpts })` returns `{ page, isDone, continueCursor }`. These standalone helpers need no Agent instance or model provider.

getPage executes the call below. Every option returns the same page, reversed for oldest-first display, and passes through result.isDone. MessageDoc has `_id` (message ID) and `order` (turn position). Clients request two messages at a time and pass getPage.continueCursor to the next call.

```ts
const result = await listMessages(ctx, components.agent, { threadId, paginationOpts });
```
questions.question: Which expression should getPage return as continueCursor?

options.rationale: The component cursor carries the traversal state expected by the next listMessages call.
A message ID is not a valid component pagination cursor.
A turn position is not the encoded component pagination cursor.
Reusing the incoming cursor does not advance traversal; the empty fallback is invalid here.
